observations.seen: Frame 1 night stadium is flat and evenly lit with no flood falloff. Frame 2 desert is a monochrome orange wash with the key nearly overhead. Frame 4 Munich has a decent bright flood but low contrast on the stands.

Player shadows are mostly soft blob decals. Frame 2 has long directional streaks, but frame 1 has none. Rectangular dark patches float on the pitch in frames 2 and 3, which look like stray shadow or decal artifacts.
There are no visible reflections or specular response on the turf, ball, kits or goal frame. Frame 3's ice gets only a single bloom hotspot rather than an environment reflection.

The crowd is made of capsule billboards in flat tiers. The scoreboard and truss textures in frames 1 and 3 look noisy and grey like placeholders. Frame 4 has decent stands, a floodlight mast and a goal.
Frame 3 snow particles are uniform blurry dots concentrated near the top of the frame. There is no indoor haze or light shafts from the floods in any frame.
Frame 1 turf uses a noisy blue-green procedural texture that reads as water. Frames 2 and 3 have flat untextured ground. Kits are unshaded flat colour.
Players are low-poly and stylized with readable silhouettes but stiff proportions. The ball is simple. The goal net in frame 4 is acceptable.
Kickoff frames are a static side-on line-up with large empty lower halves. Subjects are tiny, well under the 25–40% target. Frame 4 is better framed around the box.
The kickoff camera is low-angle and nearly flat, not the 70° broadcast pitch. Frame 4's elevated perspective works but cuts off players at the left edge.
Vignette is visible. Frame 2's orange grade crushes all separation. Frame 3's bloom hotspot is unmotivated. No tonemapping polish is apparent.
Kickoff poses are identical rigid idles. Frame 4 shows running poses that are plausible but stiff, with tiny foot-speed lines.
The scoreboard pill and controls bar are clean. However, the 'POSSESSION' label overlaps and is cut off under the score panel, and the top nav bar crowds the play view.
